sources.title: Spain is the 2026 World Cup champion, defeating Argentina for its 2nd title
FIFA World Cup 2026 Final: Argentina vs Spain live updates

chunks.text: On July 19, 2026, Spain {{pulled off}} one of the biggest wins in their history. At MetLife Stadium near New York, they {{took on}} Argentina in the final of the World Cup, the biggest event in soccer. After 90 minutes, no one had scored, so the game {{went on}} into [[extra time]]. At last, Spain won 1-0 and {{picked up}} the World Cup trophy for the second time.

verbs.wrong: To drop out of a competition
To hire someone for a job

chunks.text: For most of the match, Spain {{kept up}} the [[pressure]] and controlled the ball. Argentina's goalkeeper, Emi Martinez, was superb and made save after save. Then, deep into extra time, the [[striker]] Ferran Torres {{broke through}}. In the 106th minute, he {{put away}} a shot from close range, and Spain were in front. Martinez set a [[record]] with 11 saves, but he could not {{keep out}} every shot.

chunks.text: Argentina had dreamed of winning the World Cup two times [[in a row]]. Their [[star]], Lionel Messi, is now 39, and this was almost certainly his last World Cup. But on this night, he could not {{take over}} the game the way he once did. Spain's young players never {{let up}}, and their [[defense]] stayed strong. Argentina tried to {{fight back}}, but they could not find a way through.

chunks.text: When the final whistle went, the Spanish players fell to the ground in joy. For many fans, the win {{brought back}} happy [[memories]] of 2010, when Spain lifted their first World Cup. Sixteen years later, a new team has {{carried on}} that dream. Now Spanish soccer can {{look forward to}} a bright future, with young stars leading the way.

tf.s: Spain pulled off a 1-0 win over Argentina to take the World Cup.
tf.why: Spain pulled off a 1-0 win over Argentina in the final to win the World Cup for the second time.

tf.s: Ferran Torres put away the winning goal during extra time.
tf.why: In the 106th minute of extra time, Ferran Torres put away the shot that won the game.

tf.s: Argentina's goalkeeper kept out every single shot that Spain took.
tf.why: Emi Martinez made a record 11 saves, but he could not keep out every shot, and Spain scored.
